question: I'm a first-year IS student (P-011) entering Fall 2025. I want to take an extra course in my very first semester to accelerate my IS requirements. Is this allowed?

domain_contributions.policies: First-year students are limited to a normal course load in their first semester — overloading is explicitly prohibited for first-year students in semester 1
domain_contributions.programs: P-011's program (IS) defines what the normal first-semester course load is; typically 3-4 courses covering foundational IS and general education requirements

key_facts: Policy: 'First-years and transfer students are limited to a normal course load for their first semester of attendance'
This restriction applies regardless of student ability, advisor recommendation, or compelling academic rationale
P-011 must complete their first semester at normal load before any overload is considered
Normal IS first-semester load: typically 15-112, 67-100, English requirement, one elective (~36-45 units)
P-011 can discuss overloading from their second semester onward with their advisor
wrong_if_single_domain: Knowing only the overload policy (advisor approval sufficient for good-standing students) might suggest P-011 can overload with approval. Only by combining with the first-year-specific restriction does the correct answer emerge that NO overload is permitted in semester 1.
common_mistake: Applying the general overload policy (advisor approval = allowed) to first-year students without knowing the specific first-semester restriction
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs): P-011 is a first-year IS student in their first semester
Step 2 (policies): First-year first-semester restriction → normal load only, no exceptions
Conclusion: P-011 cannot take extra courses in their first semester regardless of advisor willingness
